_note: v2 hook overrides for the café: none needed. Every café verb is painted as the standard Monsieur Verbe mime (beret colour = verb group) and every noun shows its v1 hook, so the v1 hooks apply unchanged. v1 data is untouched.

fr_lunette_noun.hook: "lew-NEHT": LUNAR NETS! These GLASSES have two crescent MOONS for lenses: LUNAR specs.
fr_lunette_noun.why: English sound-alike LUNAR (moon) instead of French la lune; the moon-lens glasses are painted.

fr_asseoir_verb.hook: "sah-SWAHR": "SAH, SWERVE!": Monsieur Verbe SWERVES past everyone and SITS DOWN in the last free chair, admiring himself in his hand mirror.
fr_asseoir_verb.why: Complete English sound-alike; the man sitting with the mirror is painted.

fr_tasse_noun.hook: "TAHS": the laughing café boy TOSSES the CUP right off its saucer, coffee and all!
fr_tasse_noun.why: The tosser is now a boy, not a dressed mouse.

fr_cafe_noun.hook: A sleepy man in a striped nightcap hugs a cup of black COFFEE to wake up: CAFÉ, the same word as the place where you drink it.
fr_cafe_noun.why: The owl was not the hook, so it became a sleepy man in pyjamas (no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal is the hook); same change in the café shelf and in the zoom.

fr_sandwich_noun.hook: A little boy kneels on the floor and bites a giant SANDWICH, and SAND pours out of it. French says sahn-DWEETSH.

fr_serviette_noun_2.hook: A napkin folded into a swan sits by a little bell, waiting: "SERVE YET?" (sehr-VYEHT). British English even says serviette for a napkin. (In the bathroom, la serviette is the towel.)
fr_serviette_noun_2.why: RECS 1.4: napkin sense split from the towel (fr_serviette_noun, maison/bains).

fr_dire_verb.hook: "DEER": Monsieur Verbe SAYS "Bonjour!" to a little DEER on the café table, waving hello. dire = to say.
